name: Geary Residence

nadir.desc: The property consists of a single primary residence with a brown shingle roof and a multi-section footprint|A paved driveway enters from the street and widens into a turnaround beside the house|Small lawn areas sit in front of and beside the structure|Scattered trees cover the remainder of the lot on dry open ground|A public road runs along two sides of the parcel|A small detached structure is visible among the trees away from the house.

alpha.desc: The front of the residence faces Doe Lane with a paved driveway, a small lawn, and scattered trees on both sides of the drive|The house sits set back from the street|Dry open ground and tree cover occupy the rest of the frontage|A second public road runs along the side of the lot.

bravo.desc: The left side of the property shows dense scattered trees on dry open ground|The house is visible through the tree cover|The paved driveway and lawn remain near the structure|A public road runs along the outer edge of this side.

charlie.desc: The rear of the residence shows the back, surrounding trees, and dry open ground|The paved driveway and turnaround remain visible on the street side of the house|Scattered trees continue to the lot edges|No secondary public access is visible at the rear.

delta.desc: The right side of the property shows the house, the paved driveway, a small lawn, and scattered trees extending to a public road along this edge|Dry open ground occupies the ground between the trees|A small structure sits near the street corner.

considerations: Vehicle access is provided by a paved driveway from Doe Lane that widens into a turnaround beside the house. The site is a single-family residence on a wooded corner lot in a Bend-area neighborhood of similar homes. Scattered trees on dry ground surround the house and may limit some sightlines from the street. The driveway provides staging space at the front. Neighboring residences sit on adjacent wooded lots.
clarifications: Does the driveway terminate at the turnaround, or is there a path around the house? Are there any gates on the driveway? Is vehicle access available behind the house? What is the purpose of the small detached structure among the trees? How dense is the tree cover for emergency vehicle and pedestrian movement around all sides of the house?
